What have been your most educational gardening mistakes?

There have been a few for me. I took a very hippy approach to gardening when I first started and I've been trying to break myself of a few habits. Here are a few off the top of my head.

1) Digging is bad for the soil, but very necessary to establish a bed.

2) Do not underestimate weeds....ever.

3) Summer (around here) fucking sucks. Plan your garden out around the idea that you will want to spend as little time outside as possible in July/August.

4) What looks great in spring will look overgrown in Summer.

5) Start small. Better to have one small and productive garden than a yard full of plants you don't have time to manage.

6) Plan out everything. Set a date to remove certain plants and replace them with others - My gardens tend to be reactionary and not pro-active.
